This is a hand pass, and the two measurements that establish it are not a code task are the reason. First, connectivity cannot reach the remaining pixels: chair touching a thigh is inside the protection band by definition, so a component-based separation has nothing to cut. Second, no threshold divides them — the chair's mid-tones run 96 to 150 and the figure's own sub-knee edge pixels run 64 to 240, so the ranges overlap across the whole contested region.
Raising the body-tone floor to 160 was tried, rendered and reverted: it takes the feet entirely and shreds the older woman's shins. Do not propose it again as a cheaper route.

What is wanted is only what touches the body — the seat between the thighs and the chair leg against each shin — with the leg and foot contour restored underneath rather than cut around. An earlier automatic attempt removed about a pixel of the figure's own outline and the whole foot outline, which is what a threshold does to a contour and what a hand does not.
